clue.text: It may wash dirty linen dramatically on the air

definitions.text: It may wash dirty linen dramatically on the air

parts.words: It may wash dirty linen dramatically on the air
parts.note: the thing that washes is not a laundry product but a radio serial whose characters air their private quarrels in public

explanation.surface: Something launders dirty sheets with great flourish out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wash dirty linen' is the idiom for airing private scandal, and 'on the air' means broadcast; the genre was named after the detergent makers who sponsored it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running broadcast drama serial, named after its original detergent sponsors, thrives on characters' domestic scandals.

clue.text: His money is well earned

parts.note: 'well earned' reads as deserved, but means earned from a well, one drilled for petroleum

explanation.surface: A man who has truly deserved his pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A petroleum businessman makes his fortune from drilled wells.

clue.text: What an expensive little parcel could cost

definitions.text: What an expensive little parcel could cost

parts.words: What an expensive little parcel could cost
parts.note: the word for a small parcel is also British slang for a large sum of money

explanation.surface: A question about the price of a pricey small package.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost a packet' is British slang for being very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wrapped parcel shares its name with the slang for a large sum of money.

clue.text: Father gets a fit of the sulks but a sweetie

parts.note: pop is an informal name for father
a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'

explanation.surface: Dad goes into a sulk, but he is still a darling.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppet is a British term of endearment for a sweet little person, much like darling.

clue.text: More mature port produced with energy in warm surroundings

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Older port served with vigour in a cosy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' rearranges MORE, MATURE and PORT together with E for energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ambient warmth of an indoor space, around twenty degrees, is the standard temperature of a living area.

clue.text: Weapon issued without charge to independent journalist

parts.note: free means costing nothing
a lance is a long spear used by knights

explanation.surface: A weapon handed out free to a self-employed reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for several clients without a staff job; the term began with medieval mercenary knights.

clue.text: Make sure as sure can be

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: Be as confident as is possible.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, to establish a fact.

clue.text: Poor winner, maybe, but a real sport

definitions.text: Poor winner, maybe, but a real sport

parts.words: Poor winner, maybe, but a real sport
parts.note: someone poor at winning yet a true sport is one who accepts defeat graciously

explanation.surface: Someone who wins badly but is still a decent person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor winner' sounds like an ungracious victor; it means someone who seldom wins, yet takes defeat well.
explanation.definitionFit: A gracious competitor accepts being beaten with good sportsmanship.

clue.text: The others go into the Post Office quickly

indicators.note: the others are placed inside the abbreviation, so 'go into' signals one piece entering another

parts.note: PO is the standard abbreviation for Post Office
the rest means the others, those remaining

explanation.surface: Everyone else hurries into the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical tempo marking meaning fast, and also a conjuror's cry of sudden speed.

clue.text: A pond looking horribly polluted in Lancashire

definitions.note: the definition is a place found in that county, so the phrase stands for a town there

parts.note: water that looks horribly polluted is black
a pool is a small pond

explanation.surface: A filthy-looking pond somewhere in the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACKPOOL is a seaside resort town in Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The seaside resort famous for its tower and illuminations lies on the coast of that north-western county.

clue.text: Topping order to the ambitious teacher!

definitions.meaning: topping is slang for executing, especially by cutting off the head
an instruction to a teacher who wants promotion would be to become the school's chief, split as two words

explanation.surface: An excellent instruction for a schoolteacher eager to climb the career ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like the British adjective for excellent, but here it means executing; split the answer as BE HEAD for the order to an ambitious teacher, HEAD being a headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Decapitation is what topping a person means, and being made headmaster is the ambitious teacher's goal.

clue.text: Bess meant to emend the lowest of the stories

indicators.note: to emend is to correct a text, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bess intended to correct the poorest of the tales in a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emend' rearranges BESS and MEANT; 'stories' looks like tales but means floors of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellar floors below ground level are the bottom levels, or storeys, of a building.

clue.text: Military parade leaving an impression only skin-deep

definitions.meaning: an evening display of military music and marching, like the Edinburgh event
an inked design pricked into the skin is a mark made just beneath the surface

explanation.surface: A soldiers' march-past that leaves only a shallow impression on the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both an outdoor military display and an inked picture pricked into the skin.

clue.text: Solid preparation by the horticulturalist

parts.note: groundwork done with a gardener's digging tool also means thorough preliminary effort

explanation.surface: A gardener's careful groundwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard preliminary labour, like digging with a garden tool, is what makes later success possible.

clue.text: Pat and I heard assortment of popular songs

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed collection, so the letters are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Pat and I listened to a selection of chart tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment' rearranges PAT, I and HEARD; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The chart of best-selling records lists the most popular songs of the week.

clue.text: Had a celebration and got tipsy

definitions.meaning: to make merry is to celebrate with festivity
merry is British slang for slightly drunk, so this sense is became drunk

explanation.surface: Partied and drank a little too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' is British slang for mildly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrating festively and becoming slightly drunk are both expressed by the same phrase.

clue.text: Electro-magnetic unit familiar to the ornithologist

definitions.meaning: the abbreviation for electromagnetic unit, from its initials
a bird-watcher knows the large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A unit of electromagnetism that a bird expert happens to know well.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials of the physics unit spell a large flightless Australian bird that any bird scientist would know.

clue.text: Fish given food additive by the Spanish

parts.note: food additives are coded with E numbers, so E stands for one
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Fish served with a food additive by the Spaniards.
explanation.definitionFit: A long snake-like fish.

clue.text: Vessel in a Turner painting

indicators.note: the container sits inside the painter's surname, so 'in' marks letters within it

explanation.surface: A jar shown in a painting by J. M. W. Turner.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'tURNer'; Turner was a celebrated English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase-like container.

clue.text: Tommy's usual habit is to get work outside the NHS

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is slang for a British soldier, so a Tommy is a private
a practice is a usual habit or custom

explanation.surface: A British soldier's routine is to find jobs beyond the state health service.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'Tommy' is a British private soldier; the NHS is Britain's state-funded National Health Service, and doctors working outside it are paid privately.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's or dentist's fee-paying business, run independently of the state health service, is called by this name.

clue.text: One may meet him in a casual encounter

indicators.note: the man's name sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A person you might bump into by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'casuaL ENcounter'; 'him' points to a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form of Leonard is a man's name, a fellow one may meet.

clue.text: Smart little flat returned to agent retirement on retirement

indicators.note: the word for a small flat is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a pad is slang for a small flat

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the short word for an agent is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A neat little apartment is handed back to the agent when they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns PAD into DAP and 'on retirement' turns REP into PER; the first 'retirement' in the clue as printed is a duplicated word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dapper is neatly and stylishly dressed, which is one sense of smart.

clue.text: Dog seen to be reclining below a mountain-pass

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed below another follows it

parts.note: a col is a pass between mountain peaks
to lie is to be reclining

explanation.surface: A dog seen lying down beneath a high pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish sheepdog breed is called this.

clue.text: Former Chancellor may have had a close shave in his shop

definitions.meaning: Anthony ... was Chancellor of the Exchequer in the 1970s

definitions.text: may have had a close shave in his shop
definitions.meaning: a men's hairdresser gives customers a close shave on his premises

explanation.surface: An ex-finance minister had a narrow escape at his shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister; 'close shave' looks like a narrow escape but is a literal shave.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who held the Treasury's top post shares his surname with a men's hairdresser.

clue.text: Get the measure of a slightly larger dress

definitions.meaning: to assess or evaluate someone or something
a garment one size bigger is going a ...

explanation.surface: Assess whether to buy a dress a little bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess a person, and to move to a bigger garment size, are both said with this phrase.

clue.text: Looking all around while quietly cooking macaroni

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

indicators.note: cooking means the pasta's letters are being prepared into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Glancing about while silently preparing pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' looks like part of the kitchen picture but is the anagram signal; P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view takes in the whole scene in every direction.

clue.text: The chap in charge of a bunker

definitions.text: The chap in charge of a bunker

parts.words: The chap in charge of a bunker
parts.note: a bunker sounds like a golf hazard or coal store, but read as an air-raid shelter or war-time den its keeper is the official overseeing it

explanation.surface: The man responsible for a sand trap or a coal store.
explanation.walkthrough: Air-raid wardens in wartime Britain supervised shelters; the word also splits as WAR DEN, which describes a bunker.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper or supervisor of a place, such as an air-raid shelter, is given this title.

clue.text: Splendid Keep up the protest against tinned meat

parts.note: bully is an old exclamation meaning splendid, as in 'bully for you'
a beef is a complaint or protest

explanation.surface: A rousing call to keep complaining about canned meat.
explanation.walkthrough: BULLY BEEF is British canned corned beef, a soldiers' staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Corned beef sold in cans, long an army ration, goes by this name.

clue.text: They're additional passengers

definitions.meaning: clauses added to a document or verdict
people carried on a bus or horse are those who ride

explanation.surface: Extra people travelling on board.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both clauses appended to a contract and people carried on a vehicle or horse.

clue.text: Signal daily

definitions.meaning: to send a message by wire or visual signals
a newspaper published every day, this puzzle's own paper

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a long-distance signalling apparatus and a British national newspaper published each day.
